items.title: Ron Carter — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: guys who are twenty five just come out of college who are not stuck into the Henry Mancini scores, which are great.

ctx.x: Yeah, yeah. I did a couple of song tracks and from what I've seen … I've been on a couple of bands because of orchestral background tracks for movies and as I hear these producers talk to the writer of the music and the process … it's just something I don't want to do, I don't want to do that, because they don't have the musical skill verbally. They don't know how to tell you what they want. They just say, "It's not quite right, we need this more orange or need more blue or purple …." Now wait a minute. So, now…

minutes and say, "Can you play with this for ninety minutes?" "Yeah, how about just bass and percussion for ninety minutes?" We can do this, and trust my sense of musical maturity and skill, I could do that. Those projects interest me. But you need new guys, need new filmmakers to do that, guys who are twenty five just come out of college who are not stuck into the Henry Mancini scores, which are great. At the time you had a cast of thousands on the screen and a cast of five hundred in the orchestra. Well that's…
You actually won a Grammy for a composition …
